rationale:
Evidence: iteration 6 is the best design so far (465.03). Its oval track finished in 19 of 20 trials (mean 1.94 s, progress 0.99), so the course is completable at base_speed 0.9. The s-bend finished in only 4 of 20 trials (progress 0.71, max_error 0.060 m, 0.75 line-loss events per run, steering oscillation 0.38). The slalom almost never gets past progress 0.16 and always ends off track, with max_error 0.063 m. Score is dominated by the 500-point completion bonus, so converting s-bend runs into finishes is the largest available gain. Each finished run is worth roughly 900 or more. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), which is 0.06 for every allowed body width, so geometry cannot widen it. Sensor row y=0.08 is already at the forward limit, so further lead cannot come from moving the sensors.

Change: kp raised from 2.0 to 2.4, with everything else held fixed (sensor row y=0.08, x spacing 0.02 m over -0.04 to +0.04, 16 mm footprint, mass 0.6 kg, body 0.16 x 0.12 m, wheel track 0.12 m, radius 0.03 m, base_speed 0.9, ki 0, kd 1.0, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], last_direction). Reason: the s-bend and slalom errors are a large, growing lateral excursion rather than jitter, since max_error sits only just past the floor and oscillation is moderate. A stronger proportional correction should pull the robot back sooner on the bends. Check on the numbers: at a full edge signal of 2, turn is 4.8, which gives about 1680 PWM of differential, below the base PWM of about 1843 at speed 0.9, so the wheels do not reverse. kd 1.0 is kept to damp the extra gain, so the oscillation should not rise much.

Expected result: oval completion stays near 90 percent or better. The s-bend finish rate should rise above 20 percent, and s-bend progress should move toward 0.8 or more. The score should improve to roughly 500 to 600. The main risk is that kp 2.4 overshoots and raises steering oscillation, which would lower the s-bend and oval finish rates. The revision rounds should check this against the critique.
